title: Elicitation
summary: Elicitation lets a server ask the user a question in the middle of a request, through the client. Form mode collects simple structured input and URL mode sends the user out of band for anything sensitive.
useIf: A tool needs a missing, non-secret answer or a user consent that only a person can give, and the client declares support.
avoidIf: You would collect passwords, API keys, tokens or payment data in a form, or no client capability exists and nobody can answer.

explain.md: Elicitation is active, not deprecated, in 2026-07-28. A client declares `elicitation` (same as `{form: {}}`) or `url` capability, and a server MUST NOT send a mode the client did not declare [[r27]].

explain.caption: The two modes
head: Mode
What the user sees
Schema
Use for
rows: Flat object with primitive fields: string, number, boolean, single or multi-select enum
A link to open in a browser
None. The server sends a `url` and a `message`
OAuth to a third party, payments, secrets

explain.md: The user answers with an `action`: `accept` (with data in form mode), `decline` or `cancel`. Servers must handle all three and must not assume success. Form mode MUST NOT request passwords, API keys, access tokens or payment credentials, and URL mode MUST be used for them. In URL mode the client MUST show the full URL, get consent, not pre-fetch it, and open it so neither client nor model can inspect the page. Third-party credentials must never pass through the client [[r27]].

explain.title: Elicitation in 2026-07-28
explain.alt: The client calls tools/call, the server answers input_required with an elicitation request and requestState, the user answers, and the client retries with inputResponses.
explain.src:
sequenceDiagram
  participant C as Client
  participant S as Server
  C->>S: tools/call id 1
  S-->>C: input_required, elicitation, requestState
  Note over C: User answers or declines
  C->>S: tools/call id 2, inputResponses, requestState
  S-->>C: complete result

explain.md: **What changed by revision.** Form mode arrived in 2025-06-18 and URL mode in 2025-11-25 [[r31]]. In both, the server pushed `elicitation/create` on a stream within a session. In 2026-07-28 that push is gone: the request rides inside a Multi Round-Trip Request, so the server stays stateless, and `notifications/elicitation/complete` and `elicitationId` were removed [[r3]] [[r1]].

explain.title: URL mode is not login to your server
explain.md: A server MUST NOT use URL elicitation to authorize users for itself. That is what MCP authorization is for. URL mode lets the user authorize your server to reach a third party, and your server stores those tokens.

whereToUse: Disambiguation: which of three matching accounts, which region, which environment
Confirmation before an irreversible step, with an explicit decline path
Connecting a user's account at a third-party SaaS through its own consent page
Collecting a few optional parameters a tool does not need every time

use: A human is present and the client declared the capability
The answer is non-secret and fits a flat form
Third-party authorization must happen outside the client
Stateless servers should resume cleanly after the answer
avoid: Unattended or headless runs with no one to answer
Nested or complex data entry that exceeds flat primitives
flips: No elicitation capability: add the field as a tool parameter or return an actionable `isError`
The input is sensitive: switch from form to URL mode

pitfalls.symptom: A security review blocks the server
pitfalls.cause: It asked for an API key through a form-mode elicitation
pitfalls.fix: Use URL mode so the secret never transits the client or the model

pitfalls.symptom: Calls hang or fail on a headless client
pitfalls.cause: The server sent an elicitation to a client that did not declare the capability
pitfalls.fix: Read declared capabilities and fall back to parameters or an `isError` message

pitfalls.symptom: Server state breaks after a user declines
pitfalls.cause: The code assumed `accept` and used missing content
pitfalls.fix: Branch on `accept`, `decline` and `cancel` and offer alternatives

scenarios.title: Choosing among matching accounts
scenarios.situation: A `transfer` tool finds three accounts matching the user's description. A person is in the session. The choice is not sensitive.
unknowns: Could the model pick safely from account names?
scenarios.question: How do you resolve the ambiguity?

options.name: Form elicitation with a single-select enum
options.why: The user makes the choice, the server gets validated data and the flow resumes through the retry.
options.tradeoff: Requires client support and a user who responds.

options.name: Let the model pick the most likely account
options.why: A wrong guess moves money or data to the wrong target.
options.tradeoff: Acceptable only for reversible, low-stakes choices.

options.name: Ask in chat and call the tool again with an `account_id`
options.why: Works in any host with no protocol feature.
options.tradeoff: Free-form reply and no server-side validation of the choice.

flips.then: Return an `isError` message listing the choices so the model can ask in chat.

flips.if: The transfer is small, reversible and the match is exact
flips.then: Proceed without asking to avoid needless friction.

scenarios.takeaway: Let a human decide ambiguous, consequential choices.

scenarios.title: Connecting a user's SaaS account
scenarios.situation: A server needs to call a third-party API as the user. That API issues tokens through its own OAuth consent page. The MCP client must not see the tokens.
unknowns: Where will the server store tokens and how are they bound to the user?
scenarios.question: How should the user grant access?

options.name: URL elicitation to the third party's consent page
options.why: The user authorizes your server directly, outside MCP, and credentials never transit the client.
options.tradeoff: The server must hold and protect tokens keyed by verified user id.

options.name: Form elicitation asking the user to paste a token
options.why: Form mode MUST NOT be used for access tokens, and the value would pass through the client.
options.tradeoff: There is no safe case for this.

options.name: A shared service account for everyone
options.tradeoff: Loses per-user identity, audit and least privilege.

flips.if: The third party supports only service accounts
flips.then: Use a managed identity and restrict scope.
Pre-authorize through an admin portal instead.

scenarios.takeaway: Secrets and third-party consent go through URL mode.

quiz.q: A server must obtain a user's API key for a vendor. Which approach complies with the spec?
options: Form-mode elicitation with a password field
URL-mode elicitation to an out-of-band page
Put the key in the tool arguments
quiz.explain: Form mode MUST NOT collect API keys or tokens, so URL mode applies. Tool arguments pass through the model and `requestState` is attacker-controlled input that returns through the client.

quiz.q: Which actions can the user's response carry?
quiz.explain: The three actions are accept, decline and cancel. Servers must handle each. Defer and retry are not actions in the elicitation response.

flashcards.front: Which mode for passwords, API keys, tokens or payments?
flashcards.back: URL mode. Form mode MUST NOT be used for sensitive credentials.
It travels inside Multi Round-Trip Requests instead of a pushed `elicitation/create`. `notifications/elicitation/complete` and `elicitationId` were removed. It is not deprecated.

flashcards.front: What must a server do with a decline or cancel?
flashcards.back: Handle it: do not assume success, and offer alternatives or retry later.
